patterns.name: Stuck sessions showing Charging after driver left
patterns.why_grouped: Session or port state stays active (Charging, In use, or active-session block) after the driver has left or energy has stopped, mostly on FW-B 4.2.x and FW-A 3.9.0.
patterns.next_step: Apply RB-05 to each open session (T-2053 and T-2058 are triage needs_human, so check them first), and have engineering look at why session close is not registering, since earlier tickets were each closed as one-off.

patterns.name: Payment holds not released after failed or finished sessions
patterns.why_grouped: Drivers have a pending pre-authorization hold ($25 to $50) that remained after a failed, short, completed or free session.
patterns.next_step: Release each hold with RB-02 and ask engineering whether holds are failing to release automatically, which is a hypothesis only.

patterns.name: Hospital staff badges rejected after list update
patterns.why_grouped: Badges are rejected on several ports at S-038 after the host changed the badge list, and the charger auth list is v211 while the portal expects v214.
patterns.next_step: Re-push the local authorization list with RB-01 to all four S-038 chargers, confirm they reach v214, and check why the earlier push did not apply.

patterns.name: Chargers offline with no heartbeat

patterns.next_step: Run RB-03 on each, dispatch field service for CP-070-02 (no response to soft reset) and look into the repeat offline events at S-052 (T-2064).

data.symptom: Drivers see 'Charging' and idle fees running hours after unplugging, and sometimes cannot start a new session. Hosts see 'In use' on the map for an empty bay, and NOC, billing and care get alerts and disputes.
impact: 14 tickets across 9 sites and two firmware lines in 21 days
Idle fees kept running on open sessions; drivers and a fleet manager dispute them
A driver was blocked from starting a new session at another site

evidence.point: On CP-014-02 the connector reconnected and reported Available, but the backend still held the session as Charging with no Ended.
evidence.quote: state=Charging  last_meter=18.42 kWh  (no TransactionEvent Ended received)

evidence.point: On CP-031-01 the same sequence appeared after an EVCommunicationLost update and a websocket drop, and the map then showed the charger in use.
evidence.quote: CP-031-01 shown 'In use' (derived from open session)

evidence.point: On CP-022-04 an Ended did arrive after reconnect, but the backend ignored it because the connector was already Available.
evidence.quote: ignored: connector already Available (out of order)

evidence.point: On FW-B 4.2.x, 12 of 19 drops within 90 s of unplug got stuck; 41 drops at other times got none stuck.

hypotheses.statement: The backend ignores a late Ended that arrives after the connector is already Available, leaving the session open. This mechanism is seen directly in one log.
supports: CP-022-04 log shows the backend ignoring a late Ended as out of order.
Stuck cases cluster on drops within 90 s of unplug, around the reconnect.
against_or_gaps: Only one of three logs shows an Ended arriving and being ignored.
Not known whether the ignore rule is applied the same way for other firmware.

hypotheses.statement: The charger never sends or never queues the Ended after an unplug-time drop, so the backend has nothing to close the session with.
supports: CP-014-02 and CP-031-01 logs show no Ended after reconnect.
FW-B 4.2.x has the highest stuck rate: 12 of 19 drops.
against_or_gaps: A missing line at the gateway could be a capture or logging gap.
CP-022-04 (FW-A) did send an Ended, so both mechanisms may coexist.

ruled_out: Payment provider fault is unlikely: no incidents logged and normal captures on unaffected sessions.
App display bug is unlikely: the session API itself returns state=Charging.
A single bad site or charger is unlikely: 14 tickets across 9 sites.
Driver behaviour is unlikely: every affected connector reported Available within 2 minutes of unplug.
open_questions: Does the charger store and resend Ended after an unplug-time drop on FW-B 4.2.x?
Why does session-svc ignore an Ended once the connector is Available?
Could the gateway have missed Ended messages in the CP-014-02 and CP-031-01 logs?

checks.name: Each quote found in the source it cites

data.reading: Canary stuck sessions fell from 5 to 0 while drops stayed at 6; control stayed at 4 stuck. Five were closed by reconciliation, none while energy was still flowing. Direction fits the backend-ignores-late-Ended hypothesis, but counts are tiny.
what_it_does_not_prove: That FW-B fails to send queued Ended; 3 late Ended events arrived, so absence is only partial.
That the fix generalises beyond 5 canary sites on FW-B 4.2.x.
That 0 wrong closures is safe; with 5 reconciliations, a rare failure could be missed.
keep_watching: Any closure while energy still rising; late Ended applied twice.
Provisional invoice adjustments: 1 of 5 so far.
data.next_decision: Keep the canary running; do not widen yet. Bar: at least 28 more days and at least 10 further drops near unplug on canary with 0 early closures or duplicate charges. Any such event, or stuck sessions returning, reverses it.

data.title: Sessions stay open after unplug-time websocket drop
data.scope: 14 tickets (5 open, 9 closed earlier as one-offs) across 9 sites and two firmware lines (FW-B 4.2.x, FW-A 3.9.0) in 21 days.
reproduction: Run the lab reproduction test with the fix flag off: simulated charger unplugs, drops websocket, reconnects, reports Available, then sends queued Ended.
The test passes by asserting the bug: session-svc ignores the Ended as out of order and the transaction stays open.
This shows backend behaviour only. It says nothing about whether FW-B sends or queues its Ended after the drop.
Manual step: on a FW-B 4.2.x test charger, drop the connection after EVCommunicationLost but before Ended is sent; capture at charger and gateway.
evidence_attached: Lab tests: bug reproduced; regression fails without the fix
CP-022-04 log: late Ended ignored, connector already Available
CP-014-02 and CP-031-01 logs: Available after reconnect, no Ended
Fleet view: FW-B 4.2.x 12 of 19 stuck; 41 other drops, 0 stuck
Unplug-to-drop times for 14 stuck sessions, all 3 to 88 s
ruled_out: Payment provider fault: unlikely, no incidents and normal captures on unaffected sessions
App display bug: unlikely, session API itself returns state=Charging
Single bad site or charger: unlikely, 14 tickets across 9 sites
Driver behaviour: unlikely, every connector reported Available within 2 minutes of unplug
data.workaround_in_place: Support corrected the 5 open sessions with RB-05 at last meter value and reversed idle fees; invoice flagged for billing review; a 15-minute detector query is proposed, not yet running.
data.the_ask: Decide whether to change session-svc to accept a late Ended after the connector is Available, and to approve the 15-minute detector until the fix ships. Also assign the FW-B 4.2.x capture test.
data.hypothesis_note: The backend ignoring a late Ended is reproduced in a lab with a simulated charger. Whether FW-B drops its queued Ended is not confirmed.

checks.name: Lab test attached; firmware question marked not confirmed

data.title: Session stuck Charging after unplug websocket drop
applies_when: Driver sees Charging and idle fees running hours after unplugging
Host map shows In use on an empty bay
Driver cannot start a new session after a recent unplug
how_to_confirm: In the charger log, find a websocket drop within 90 s of unplug, then Available after reconnect.
Late-Ended form: session-svc log shows 'ignored: connector already Available (out of order)', as on CP-022-04.
No-Ended form: log shows state=Charging, no TransactionEvent Ended received, after reconnect, as on CP-014-02 and CP-031-01.
steps: Confirm the meter shows no energy change since unplug, before RB-05.
Run RB-05 at the last meter value to close the session and reverse idle fees.
If a payment hold remains, check the session is closed, then use RB-02.
Flag the invoice for billing review and link the ticket to the parent incident.
escalate_if: Energy is still rising on the open session.
No connection drop occurred near the unplug time.
Charger runs a firmware line other than FW-A or FW-B.
A newer session already started on the same connector.
data.status_note: ENG-4471 is behind a per-station flag on 5 FW-B canary sites with 6 control sites; whether FW-B sends or queues Ended after reconnect is unconfirmed, vendor ticket open.
